title: Acceleration
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, sci-speed-velocity-acceleration, is broader than the new point because it also teaches speed and velocity, and it does not mention that acceleration is the slope of a velocity-time graph, which the brief names, so no bank point matches it exactly.

draft.title: Acceleration
card: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time taken.
It is measured in metres per second squared (m/s²). An acceleration of 2 m/s² means velocity changes by 2 m/s every second.
Velocity changes when an object speeds up, slows down or changes direction. Slowing down gives a negative acceleration when the motion is in the positive direction.
On a velocity-time graph, acceleration is the slope of the line. A steeper line means a bigger acceleration, and a flat line means zero acceleration.

4.alt: A velocity-time graph. A straight line rises from 0 m/s at 0 s to 12 m/s at 4 s, so its slope is 3 m/s squared.

draft.remember: Acceleration is change in velocity per second, and it is the slope of a velocity-time graph.

a.q: A scooter in Hobart speeds up from 2 m/s to 12 m/s in 5 seconds. What is its acceleration?
a.why: Change in velocity is 12 - 2 = 10 m/s. Dividing by 5 s gives 2 m/s². Using 12 ÷ 5 ignores the starting velocity, which gives 2.4 m/s².
a.clue: Find the change in velocity first.

b.q: On a velocity-time graph, a train's line runs flat at 20 m/s for 30 seconds. What is the train's acceleration during this time?
opts: Zero, because its velocity is not changing
20 m/s², because its velocity is 20 m/s
Zero, because the train is not moving
b.why: A flat line has zero slope, so the acceleration is zero. The train is moving at a steady 20 m/s, but its velocity does not change. Acceleration depends on change in velocity, not on how big the velocity is.
b.clue: What is the slope of a flat line?

b.best: Zero, because its velocity is not changing
